attempted_axis: move_logic15 exact closure: re-measure the two blocking stack slots from the aligned disassembly (which INVERTED the prior pass's attribution of them), then place both by MWCC's declaration-order rule - hoist the volatile f32 truncation temp to function scope between the pad and ady, and conserve the 48-byte pad total by splitting 8 bytes off into a second pad declared LAST so the local block's bottom anchor shifts up without growing the frame.

axis_log: MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, and it is the whole reason this function closed: the prior record's identification of the two blocking slot groups is INVERTED, and its instruction opcodes are wrong. Read from `fnasm.py game/enemy/enemy.c move_logic15 0x0:0x35c --diff`, the six blocking words are: (a) +0x2e8 stfs / +0x2f0 lwz / +0x2f8 stw / +0x2fc lfs, ours 64(r1) vs target 20(r1) - these are NOT the volatile tmp, they are `f32 ady` and its bit-trick abs (`ady = dy; *(u32*)&ady &= 0x7FFFFFFF`), whose stfs/lwz/clrlwi/stw/lfs signature is unmistakable; (b) +0x270 stfs / +0x274 lfs, ours 12(r1) vs target 24(r1) - THIS is the volatile f32 tmp round-trip, and it is stfs/lfs (32-bit), not the 'stfd/lfd f64 compiler scratch' the prior record named. There is no f64 stack scratch anywhere in this function. Because the prior pass believed tmp sat at 0x40, its four 'pad axis' probes were steering the wrong variable, which is why they read as inert.

AXIS 1 (the model): target's local block is ady at 0x14, tmp at 0x18, then 48 bytes to 0x4b, ending EXACTLY at the stmw r29,76(r1) boundary. Ours was tmp 0x0c, pad 0x10-0x3f, ady 0x40. Declaration order was ady, pad, tmp(inner-block). Ascending address therefore equals REVERSE declaration order: first-declared gets the highest address, and an inner-block local sits below every function-scope local. To get target's ascending ady, tmp, pad the declaration order must be pad, tmp, ady.

AXIS 2 (NEUTRAL on real, but the decisive structural step): hoist `volatile f32 tmp` out of the inner if-block to function scope and order the declarations `u8 _pad15[48]; volatile f32 tmp; f32 ady;`. real stayed 104 - but the slots MOVED exactly as the model predicts: ady 0x40 -> 0x0c and tmp 0x0c -> 0x10. The relative order was now target-correct (ady immediately below tmp, 4 bytes apart); the whole block simply sat 8 bytes too low. This is why `real` is a poor arbiter for slot work: it was flat across a change that solved the ordering half of the problem.

AXIS 3 (REGRESSED 104 -> 108, discarded, but highly informative): append `u8 _pad15b[8]` declared LAST to shift the block up 8. All SIX blocking displacement words CLOSED - tmp 24(r1)=24(r1) and ady 20(r1)=20(r1), exactly target. The cost was that the frame grew 88 -> 96 (stwu -96, stmw r29,84), opening 4 NEW blocking words. Net displacement words 6 -> 4. This proved the 8 bytes sitting above the pad at 0x44-0x4b are NOT reclaimable slack.

AXIS 4 (EXACT, RETAINED): conserve the pad total instead of adding to it - `u8 _pad15[40]; volatile f32 tmp; f32 ady; u8 _pad15b[8];`, i.e. move 8 bytes from the high pad into a new low pad declared last. 40+4+4+8 = 56 = the original 48+4+4. Frame stayed 88, stmw r29,76 matched, and ady landed at 20(r1) and tmp at 24(r1) - every stack word in the function now identical to target. real 104 -> 98, insns 215/215, multiset IDENTICAL, and the entire remaining residual was FPR/GPR renaming. Committed 622710503.

AXIS 5 (EXACT): with the STACK_LAYOUT residual gone the function is a pure renaming bisimulation, so webfrank_audit now derives it cleanly - REGISTER_ONLY, 215 instructions, plain copy_register_fields with NO unproven_recolor_audit note. Positive control that the guard is discriminating rather than rubber-stamping: the same audit run REJECTED sibling move_logic00 with 'use of f29 does not correspond to f30 under the running renaming'. Rule added for move_logic15 ONLY (this lane's claim); real 98 -> 0, fuzzy 100.0000%. Committed 6941d37a0.

The volatile is load-bearing and correct: it produces target's own stfs 24(r1)/lfs 24(r1) truncation round-trip at +0x270/+0x274, which is present in the RETAIL bytes.
